✓ Environment & Climate.question: Which is the main environmental protection act in India?
✓ Environment & Climate.fact: Environment Protection Act, 1986. The Environment Protection Act 1986 is the umbrella legislation enacted after the Bhopal gas tragedy (1984), empowering the Centre to protect and improve the environment.

✓ Environment & Climate.question: Which act deals with air pollution control in India?
✓ Environment & Climate.answer: Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981
✓ Environment & Climate.fact: Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981. The Air Act 1981, passed after the 1972 Stockholm Conference, prevents and controls air pollution and is implemented through the CPCB.

✓ Environment & Climate.question: Which act deals with water pollution control in India?
✓ Environment & Climate.answer: Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974
✓ Environment & Climate.fact: Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974. The Water Act 1974 was India’s first pollution-control law and established the CPCB and state pollution control boards.

✓ Environment & Climate.fact: Wild Life Protection Act, 1972. The Wild Life Protection Act 1972 protects wild animals, birds and plants, and provides the legal basis for national parks and sanctuaries.

✓ Equilibrium thermodynamics.fact: For example, a chemical reaction at constant temperature and pressure will reach equilibrium at a minimum of its components' Gibbs free energy and a maximum of their entropy.

✓ Equine nutrition.subject: Environment & Ecology
✓ Equine nutrition.question: What do you know about Equine nutrition?
✓ Equine nutrition.answer: the feeding of horses, ponies, mules, donkeys, and other equines.
✓ Equine nutrition.fact: Equine nutrition is the feeding of horses, ponies, mules, donkeys, and other equines.

✓ Equine nutrition.subject: Environment & Ecology
✓ Equine nutrition.question: These include calcium, phosphorus, sodium, potassium, and _____, and are commonly found in most good-quality feeds
✓ Equine nutrition.fact: These include calcium, phosphorus, sodium, potassium, and chloride, and are commonly found in most good-quality feeds. Normally, if adult animals at maintenance levels are consuming fresh hay or are on pasture, they will receive adequate amounts of minerals in their diet, with the exception of sodium chloride (salt), which needs to be provided, preferably free choice.

✓ Equine nutrition.subject: Environment & Ecology
✓ Equine nutrition.question: Some pastures are deficient in certain trace minerals, including selenium, zinc, and copper, and in such situations, _____, including deficiency diseases, may occur if horses' trace mineral intake is not properly supplemented
✓ Equine nutrition.fact: Some pastures are deficient in certain trace minerals, including selenium, zinc, and copper, and in such situations, health problems, including deficiency diseases, may occur if horses' trace mineral intake is not properly supplemented.

✓ Equine nutrition.subject: Environment & Ecology
✓ Equine nutrition.question: Some commonly used grasses include timothy, brome, fescue, coastal _____, orchard grass, and Kentucky bluegrass
✓ Equine nutrition.fact: Some commonly used grasses include timothy, brome, fescue, coastal Bermuda, orchard grass, and Kentucky bluegrass.

✓ Equine nutrition.subject: Environment & Ecology
✓ Equine nutrition.question: Corn (USA), or maize (_____), is the second most palatable grain
✓ Equine nutrition.fact: Corn (USA), or maize (British English), is the second most palatable grain.

✓ Equine nutrition.subject: Environment & Ecology
✓ Equine nutrition.question: It is frequently fed in combination with oats and corn, a mix informally referred to by the acronym "COB" (for Corn, Oats and _____)
✓ Equine nutrition.fact: Barley is also fed to horses, but needs to be processed to crack the seed hull and allow easier digestibility. It is frequently fed in combination with oats and corn, a mix informally referred to by the acronym "COB" (for Corn, Oats and Barley).

✓ Equine nutrition.subject: Environment & Ecology
✓ Equine nutrition.question: Grain mixes with added molasses are usually called "sweet feed" in the _____ and "coarse mix" in the United Kingdom
✓ Equine nutrition.fact: Grain mixes with added molasses are usually called "sweet feed" in the United States and "coarse mix" in the United Kingdom.

✓ Equine nutrition.subject: Environment & Ecology
✓ Equine nutrition.question: Too high an NSC level causes difficulties for animals prone to laminitis or equine polysaccharide storage myopathy (_____)
✓ Equine nutrition.fact: Too high an NSC level causes difficulties for animals prone to laminitis or equine polysaccharide storage myopathy (EPSM).

✓ Equine nutrition.subject: Environment & Ecology
✓ Equine nutrition.question: Not only can excess grain and inadequate exercise lead to behavior problems, it may also trigger serious health problems that include _____, or "tying up", in horses prone to the condition
✓ Equine nutrition.fact: Not only can excess grain and inadequate exercise lead to behavior problems, it may also trigger serious health problems that include Equine Exertional Rhabdomyolysis, or "tying up", in horses prone to the condition.

✓ Equine nutrition.subject: Environment & Ecology
✓ Equine nutrition.question: The small intestine is 50 to _____ (15 to 21 m) long and holds 10 US gallons (38 L) to 12 US gallons (45 L)
✓ Equine nutrition.fact: The small intestine is 50 to 70 feet (15 to 21 m) long and holds 10 US gallons (38 L) to 12 US gallons (45 L).

✓ Equine nutrition.subject: Environment & Ecology
✓ Equine nutrition.question: It is also known as the "water gut" or "hind gut." It is a blind-ended pouch, about _____ (1.2 m) long that holds 7 US gallons (26 L) to 8 US gallons (30 L)
✓ Equine nutrition.fact: It is also called the "water gut" or "hind gut." It is a blind-ended pouch, about 4 feet (1.2 m) long that holds 7 US gallons (26 L) to 8 US gallons (30 L).

✓ Equine nutrition.subject: Environment & Ecology
✓ Equine nutrition.question: The large colon is 10 to _____ (3.0 to 3.7 m) long and holds up to 20 US gallons (76 L) of semi-liquid matter
✓ Equine nutrition.fact: The large colon is 10 to 12 feet (3.0 to 3.7 m) long and holds up to 20 US gallons (76 L) of semi-liquid matter. The small colon is also 10 to 12 feet (3.0 to 3.7 m) long, holds about 5 US gallons (19 L), is the area where the majority of water is absorbed, and where fecal balls are formed.

✓ Equine nutrition.subject: Environment & Ecology
✓ Equine nutrition.question: The small colon is also 10 to _____ (3.0 to 3.7 m) long, holds about 5 US gallons (19 L), is the area where the majority of water is absorbed, and where fecal balls are formed
✓ Equine nutrition.fact: The large colon is 10 to 12 feet (3.0 to 3.7 m) long and holds up to 20 US gallons (76 L) of semi-liquid matter. The small colon is also 10 to 12 feet (3.0 to 3.7 m) long, holds about 5 US gallons (19 L), is the area where the majority of water is absorbed, and where fecal balls are formed.

✓ Equine nutrition.subject: Environment & Ecology
✓ Equine nutrition.question: Horses can only live a few days without water, becoming dangerously dehydrated if they lose 8-_____ of their natural body water
✓ Equine nutrition.fact: Horses can only live a few days without water, becoming dangerously dehydrated if they lose 8-10% of their natural body water.

✓ Equine nutrition.subject: Environment & Ecology
✓ Equine nutrition.question: An average 1,000-pound (_____) horse drinks 10 to 12 US gallons (38–45 L) of water per day, more in hot weather, when eating dry forage such as hay, or when consuming high levels of salt, potassium, a
✓ Equine nutrition.fact: An average 1,000-pound (450 kg) horse drinks 10 to 12 US gallons (38–45 L) of water per day, more in hot weather, when eating dry forage such as hay, or when consuming high levels of salt, potassium, and magnesium.

✓ Equine nutrition.subject: Environment & Ecology
✓ Equine nutrition.question: Horses can benefit from up to _____ fat in their diets, but more does not always provide a visible benefit
✓ Equine nutrition.fact: Horses can benefit from up to 8% fat in their diets, but more does not always provide a visible benefit.

✓ Equine nutrition.subject: Environment & Ecology
✓ Equine nutrition.question: Horses can only have 15-_____ fat in their diet without the risk of developing diarrhea
✓ Equine nutrition.fact: Horses can only have 15-20% fat in their diet without the risk of developing diarrhea.

✓ Equine nutrition.subject: Environment & Ecology
✓ Equine nutrition.question: The SCFAs produced in the hindgut provide up to _____ of the horse's energy needs
✓ Equine nutrition.fact: The SCFAs produced in the hindgut provide up to 70% of the horse's energy needs.

✓ Equine nutrition.subject: Environment & Ecology
✓ Equine nutrition.question: Digestible carbohydrates are found in nearly every feed source; corn has the highest amount, with an average starch content of _____, then barley and oats
✓ Equine nutrition.fact: Digestible carbohydrates are found in nearly every feed source; corn has the highest amount, with an average starch content of 72%, then barley and oats.

✓ Equine nutrition.subject: Environment & Ecology
✓ Equine nutrition.question: Forages normally have only 6-_____ soluble carbohydrate, but under certain conditions can have up to 30%
✓ Equine nutrition.fact: Forages normally have only 6-8% soluble carbohydrate, but under certain conditions can have up to 30%.

✓ Equine nutrition.subject: Environment & Ecology
✓ Equine nutrition.question: Most adult horses only require 8-_____ protein in their diet; however, higher protein is important for lactating mares and young growing foals
✓ Equine nutrition.fact: Most adult horses only require 8-10% protein in their diet; however, higher protein is important for lactating mares and young growing foals.

✓ Equine nutrition.subject: Environment & Ecology
✓ Equine nutrition.question: Therefore, a 1,000 lb (_____) adult horse could eat up to 25 lb (11 kg) of food
✓ Equine nutrition.fact: Therefore, a 1,000 lb (450 kg) adult horse could eat up to 25 lb (11 kg) of food.

✓ Equine nutrition.subject: Environment & Ecology
✓ Equine nutrition.question: Foals less than six months of age eat 2–_____ of their weight each day
✓ Equine nutrition.fact: Foals less than six months of age eat 2–4% of their weight each day.

✓ Equine nutrition.subject: Environment & Ecology
✓ Equine nutrition.question: Equine nutritionists recommend that _____ or more of the animal's diet by weight should be forages
✓ Equine nutrition.fact: Equine nutritionists recommend that 50% or more of the animal's diet by weight should be forages.

✓ Equine nutrition.subject: Environment & Ecology
✓ Equine nutrition.question: However, forage amount should never go below _____ of the horse's body weight per day
✓ Equine nutrition.fact: However, forage amount should never go below 1% of the horse's body weight per day.

✓ Equine nutrition.subject: Environment & Ecology
✓ Equine nutrition.question: Soybean meal is a common protein supplement, and averages about _____ crude protein
✓ Equine nutrition.fact: Soybean meal is a common protein supplement, and averages about 44% crude protein.

✓ Equine nutrition.subject: Environment & Ecology
✓ Equine nutrition.question: For example, 1 lb (_____) of oats has a different volume than 1 lb (0.45 kg) of corn
✓ Equine nutrition.fact: For example, 1 lb (0.45 kg) of oats has a different volume than 1 lb (0.45 kg) of corn.

✓ Equine nutrition.subject: Environment & Ecology
✓ Equine nutrition.question: It is safe to feed a ration that is _____ forage (along with water and supplemental salt), and any feed ration should be at least 50% forage
✓ Equine nutrition.fact: It is safe to feed a ration that is 100% forage (along with water and supplemental salt), and any feed ration should be at least 50% forage.

✓ Equine nutrition.subject: Environment & Ecology
✓ Equine nutrition.question: When beet pulp is fed, a ration of 2 lb (_____) to 5 lb (2.3 kg) is usually soaked in water for 3 to 4 hours prior to feeding in order to make it more palatable, and to minimize the risk of choke and
✓ Equine nutrition.fact: When beet pulp is fed, a ration of 2 lb (0.91 kg) to 5 lb (2.3 kg) is usually soaked in water for 3 to 4 hours prior to feeding in order to make it more palatable, and to minimize the risk of choke and other problems.

✓ Equine nutrition.subject: Environment & Ecology
✓ Equine nutrition.question: However, even these rations should have some hay or pasture provided, a minimum of a half-pound of forage for every 100 lb (_____) of horse, in order to keep the digestive system functioning properly
✓ Equine nutrition.fact: However, even these rations should have some hay or pasture provided, a minimum of a half-pound of forage for every 100 lb (45 kg) of horse, in order to keep the digestive system functioning properly and to meet the horse's urge to graze.

✓ Equine nutrition.subject: Environment & Ecology
✓ Equine nutrition.question: Equine gastric ulcer syndrome is linked to a too-high concentration of grain in the diet, particularly noticed in modern racehorses, where some studies show such ulcers affecting up to _____ of all ra
✓ Equine nutrition.fact: Equine gastric ulcer syndrome is linked to a too-high concentration of grain in the diet, particularly noticed in modern racehorses, where some studies show such ulcers affecting up to 90% of all race horses.

✓ Equine nutrition.subject: Environment & Ecology
✓ Equine nutrition.question: In general, the portion of the ration that should be grain or other concentrated feed is 0-_____ grain for mature idle horses; between 20-70% for horses at work, depending on age, intensity of activit
✓ Equine nutrition.fact: In general, the portion of the ration that should be grain or other concentrated feed is 0-10% grain for mature idle horses; between 20-70% for horses at work, depending on age, intensity of activity, and energy requirements.

✓ Equine nutrition.subject: Environment & Ecology
✓ Equine nutrition.question: Forages may be fed based on weight, at a rate of about 1 lb (_____) of forage for every 100 lb (45 kg)
✓ Equine nutrition.fact: Forages may be fed based on weight, at a rate of about 1 lb (0.45 kg) of forage for every 100 lb (45 kg).

✓ Equine nutrition.subject: Environment & Ecology
✓ Equine nutrition.question: If a hard-working pony needs concentrates, a ratio of no more than _____ concentrates to 70% forage is recommended
✓ Equine nutrition.fact: If a hard-working pony needs concentrates, a ratio of no more than 30% concentrates to 70% forage is recommended.

✓ Equine nutrition.subject: Environment & Ecology
✓ Equine nutrition.question: They only need to eat _____ of their body weight per day in dry matter
✓ Equine nutrition.fact: They only need to eat 1.5% of their body weight per day in dry matter.

✓ Equine nutrition.subject: Environment & Ecology

✓ Equine nutrition.fact: (See § Illnesses related to improper feeding below) It is generally not safe to give a horse feed that was contaminated by the remains of a dead animal.

✓ Equine nutrition.subject: Environment & Ecology
✓ Equine nutrition.question: This pattern of clinical signs led to the archaic nickname "_____ morning sickness"
✓ Equine nutrition.fact: This pattern of clinical signs led to the archaic nickname "Monday morning sickness".
